title: Comparison of one saturated log blowup with normalization
statement:
Let $(X,M)$ be a log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] with $X$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $\mathcal I\subset M$ be a nonempty coherent log ideal, and put $J=\alpha(\mathcal I)\mathcal O_X$. Then $J$ is a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, and the saturated log blowup $b:(X',M')\to(X,M)$ exists and is log regular. Its underlying scheme morphism is canonically isomorphic over $X$ to
$$\bigl(\operatorname{Bl}_J X\bigr)^\nu\longrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}_J X\longrightarrow X,$$
where the superscript $\nu$ means normalization in the function field [def-sc-normalization], and the ordinary blowup is locally the scheme covered, for a finite set of ideal generators $a$, by $\operatorname{Spec}A[J/a]$ with $A[J/a]\subset A_a$ the subalgebra generated by $j/a$, $j\in J$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring, prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover]. If $U$ is the triviality locus of $(X,M)$, then $b^{-1}U\to U$ is an isomorphism and the triviality locus of $(X',M')$ is exactly $b^{-1}U$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.4.1--3.4.6(i), printed pp. 110--111 (monoidal ideals and normalized-blowup comparison); 3.3.8--3.3.11, printed pp. 107--108, and Expose VI, 1.8, printed p. 70 (log regularity preserved). The triviality-locus assertion is the universal property over U and the local homomorphism on local rings outside U.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction], $J$ is finite type and quasi-coherent. By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure], $U$ is open dense and every log section is a unit on $U$. The nonempty log ideal therefore gives $J|_U=\mathcal O_U$, so $J\ne0$.

Use [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction] to obtain the fine blowup $X_0$, the fs blowup $X'$, and finite $s:X'\to X_0$. The fs universal property is [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Its strict etale local saturated charts are $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_h^{\rm sat}]$ with finitely generated saturated $Q_h^{\rm sat}\subset P^{\rm gp}$ and the same group completion. By [lem-trf-log-regular-toric-refinement] each is locally Noetherian and log regular; these strict etale local conditions give the same properties for $X'$.

Cover $X$ by strict etale charts $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. By the strict etale restriction and pullback clauses of [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction], $X_0\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is the fine log blowup of the chart and $J\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A_i}=(\alpha(h):h\in E)$, $E$ finite nonempty; [lem-trf-monomial-rees-chart-comparison] identifies it with the ordinary blowup of that ideal. Each $\alpha(h)$ is a non-zero-divisor: by [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure] it is a unit on a dense open and local rings are domains; a zero germ would vanish on a neighbourhood meeting it, so multiplication is injective on stalks. Thus [lem-trf-etale-blowup-chart-descent] applies to $Z=X_0$ and gives a canonical $X$-isomorphism $X_0\simeq B=\operatorname{Bl}_JX$. In particular $s:X'\to B$ is finite.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.4.6(i); Stacks 0805, 0806, 022C, 023Q, through the two cited comparison lemmas.

proof.text: Over $U$, every element of $M$ is a unit. Thus $\mathcal I|_U=M|_U$, an ideal generated by the identity. The identity of $U$ has the fs universal property, so [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] identifies the restriction $b^{-1}U\to U$ with the identity as a log scheme. In particular its log structure is trivial. Conversely take a geometric point $x'\in X'$ with image $x\notin U$. There exists $m\in M_{\bar x}$ with nonunit structural image in $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$; otherwise the defining inverse-image-of-units condition of a log structure would make its characteristic zero. The induced homomorphism of strict local rings is local, so the image of $\alpha(m)$ is in the maximal ideal at $x'$. Its log section in $M'_{\bar x'}$ is thus not a unit, by the same condition. As $x'\notin b^{-1}U$ was arbitrary, the triviality locus of $M'$ is exactly $b^{-1}U$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.9; universal property and local-ring argument.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure], $X'$ has normal domain local rings and dense triviality locus. The preceding step identifies that locus with $b^{-1}U\simeq U$. $U\ne\emptyset$, being dense in integral $X$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-normal-blowup-recognition] to $s:X'\to B$ and $U$: all its hypotheses were proved above. It gives integrality of $B$ and $X'$, surjectivity of $s$, the common field $k(X)$, and the canonical normalization identification $X'\simeq B^\nu$ over $B$, hence over $X$.

source.place: VIII 3.4.6(i); VI 1.4 and VIII 3.5; finite normal-model recognition.

lean.statement: theorem exists_saturatedLogBlowup_normalization (X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X.scheme] (hX : X.IsLogRegular) (I : X.logStructure.IdealFamily) (hI : X.logStructure.IsNonemptyCoherentIdeal I) : ∃ J : X.scheme.IdealSheafData, (∀ (V : X.scheme.affineOpens) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X.scheme) (w : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t).fiber.obj (Scheme.Etale.mk V.1.ι)), (J.ideal V).map ((strictLocalGerm X.scheme t (Scheme.Etale.mk V.1.ι) w).hom.comp V.1.topIso.inv.hom) = Ideal.span (X.logStructure.toEtalePrelogStructure.stalkAlpha t '' X.logStructure.idealStalk I t)) ∧ J ≠ ⊥ ∧ J.ofFiniteType ∧ ∃ hB : IsIntegral J.blowup, ∃ (X' : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (b : EtaleLogHom X' X), IsSaturatedLogBlowup b I ∧ X'.IsLogRegular ∧ (∃! e : X'.scheme ≅ @Scheme.normalization J.blowup hB, e.hom ≫ @Scheme.fromNormalization J.blowup hB ≫ J.blowupMap = b.base) ∧ ∃ U : X.scheme.Opens, (U : Set X.scheme) = X.logStructure.trivialityLocus ∧ IsIso (b.base ∣_ U) ∧ X'.logStructure.trivialityLocus = b.base ⁻¹' (U : Set X.scheme)
lean.note: The monoidal ideal is existentially specified by equality of its extensions to every geometric stalk with the span of structural images of the log ideal. This characterizes the actual ideal α(I) O_X, including étale-only local generators; no object is selected from an existence proof. The integral-blowup witness supplies the instance required by Scheme.normalization. The open U is the triviality locus, and the normalization comparison is unique over X.
